original_question: If a measure-preserving automorphism is mixing, must it satisfy light twofold mixing? Here light twofold mixing means that for every sequences m_i, n_i -> +infinity and every measurable sets A, B, C of positive measure, one has lim sup_i mu(A intersect T^{m_i}B intersect T^{m_i+n_i}C) > 0.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1: whether every mixing measure-preserving automorphism is lightly 2-mixing.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the main mathematical target of Conjecture 1.1: it asks whether ordinary mixing for a measure-preserving automorphism forces the paper’s weaker triple-correlation property called light 2-mixing, and it correctly includes the quantifiers over arbitrary positive-measure sets A, B, C and arbitrary sequences m_i, n_i tending to +infinity.
missing_details: The ambient setting should be stated explicitly: T is an automorphism of a standard probability space (X, B, mu).
Because the paper speaks about an automorphism, T should be understood as invertible and measure-preserving.
The sequences m_i and n_i should be specified as integer (equivalently, natural) sequences with m_i -> +infinity and n_i -> +infinity.
To make the question stand-alone, the usual definition of mixing should be included: mu(A ∩ T^n B) -> mu(A)mu(B) for all measurable A, B.
The positivity assumptions should be written as mu(A) > 0, mu(B) > 0, mu(C) > 0.
The paper’s exact terminology is 'lightly 2-mixing' (or light 2-mixing), so that phrase should be preferred over a looser paraphrase.
Proposition 1.2 gives a paper-internal equivalent reformulation, so the sharpened version should note that equivalence rather than leave the definition isolated.
The question is conjectural/open in the paper, so the refined wording should preserve that scope and not broaden it to full higher-order mixing.
refined_question: Let T be a mixing measure-preserving automorphism of a standard probability space (X, B, mu), meaning that for all measurable sets D, E in B one has mu(D ∩ T^n E) -> mu(D)mu(E) as n -> +infinity. Must T be lightly 2-mixing; that is, for every pair of integer sequences m_i, n_i -> +infinity and every measurable sets A, B, C in B with mu(A), mu(B), mu(C) > 0, does one necessarily have limsup_{i->infinity} mu(A ∩ T^{m_i}B ∩ T^{m_i+n_i}C) > 0?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently (as reformulated in Proposition 1.2), is it enough to require that for every measurable set A with mu(A) > 0 and every integer sequences m_i, n_i -> +infinity, one has limsup_{i->infinity} mu(A ∩ T^{m_i}A ∩ T^{m_i+n_i}A) > 0?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s intended question: it matches the subject and quantifier structure of Conjecture 1.1. The main repairs are to make the probability-space setting and the meaning of 'mixing automorphism' explicit, and to align the terminology with the paper’s 'lightly 2-mixing'. Proposition 1.2 is the key nearby sharpening because it supplies the equivalent one-set reformulation, so the refined question should stay at exactly that level and not drift to a broader multiple-mixing problem. Theorem 1.3 is part of the same opening discussion in Section 1 and is cited because the paper treats it as immediate context for this conjectural light 2-mixing question.
